Play report

I reached level 4 of 6 and did not beat the game: levels 1–3 are beaten, and level 4 ended in GAME_OVER when the move timer ran out.

**How the game works, as far as I worked it out:**
- **Movement:** you steer a 4×4 piece with actions 1–4 (up, down, left, right).
- **Panel:** clicking cells in the bottom-right 3×3 panel turns them on or off. When the cells you've turned on match a pattern shown on the left of the screen, that pattern's effect fires. The four edge cells shrink the piece to 2×2. Another pattern moves the piece into a marked area. The middle column fires a beam that can destroy a 6-coloured box, which opens a gate.
- **Goal:** move the piece into the 9/a-coloured socket.
- **Timer:** the bar on the right shrinks with every action. In level 4 it only allows about 16 actions, and the game ends when it empties.

**Why level 4 failed:** I fired the beam upward to open the gate, but at the piece's width it hit the region's top wall and never reached the box. Moving through 4-cell steps, the full-size piece can't line up with the narrow channel leading up to the box. Most likely the fix is to shrink the piece first and then fire. I didn't have enough actions left to try that.

I didn't call /reset. My notes for another attempt are in `NOTES.md` in the working directory.

Round interview

**1. What happened on level 4**

The 4×4 piece sits in a room. The exit socket is to the right, behind a gate. Earlier levels showed that firing the beam (the middle-column panel pattern) at a box with a 6-coloured border destroys the box and opens the gate. On level 4 that box sits above the room at the top of a narrow 2-cell-wide channel (columns 31–32). The 4×4 piece moves in 4-cell steps, so it can only stand at x = 21, 25, 29, 33…. It can never line up exactly with that channel.

I stood at x=29 and fired upward. The 4-wide beam stopped at the room's top wall and didn't hurt the box. That cost about 7 of the level's roughly 16 actions. I then walked onto a 2×2 `ee` item, hoping it was a timer refill. It wasn't, at least not when covered by the full-size piece. I spent the last actions confirming that the beam fired right just stops at the room wall and doesn't open the gate. The timer emptied and the next action ended the game.

The cause was spending budget on an untested idea, firing while unaligned, when the level is tight. The underlying mistake was not seeing that the piece had to be shrunk first.

**2. Is it still winnable?**

I think so, but I haven't confirmed it. The intended route is probably:
- Shrink the piece with the four-edge pattern. The 2×2 piece moves in 2-cell steps, so it can reach x=31 under the channel.
- Face up and fire, so the 2-wide beam goes up the channel and destroys the box, which opens the gate.
- Travel right through the gate to the socket. On level 1 a 2×2 piece won by entering a 4×4 socket.

The difficulty is cost. Roughly: shrink takes 4 clicks, moving into line about 3, turning up 1, firing 3, which is about 11 actions. The 2×2 piece then needs about 14 more moves to reach the socket at 2 cells per step. That totals roughly 25 actions against a budget of about 16. So the plan only fits if one of these holds:
- (a) Clicking the shrink pattern again restores 4×4 size cheaply.
- (b) The `ee` item refills the timer when the 2×2 piece overlaps it exactly.
- (c) Actions cost less than I measured.

I haven't checked any of these. Measured costs varied: moves took about 3–4 timer rows each and clicks about 4–5, out of 64 rows.

What would settle it:
- the timer cost of each action type;
- where the 2×2 piece lands after shrinking (on level 1 it kept the top-left corner);
- whether the 2×2 piece can land exactly on the `ee` cells (x 23–24, y 34–35) and what that does;
- whether repeating the four-edge pattern grows the piece back.

**3. Next attempt**

1. Shrink immediately, then read the timer after every action to get exact costs.
2. If the 2×2 piece can reach the `ee` item cheaply, take it and see whether the timer refills.
3. Line up at x=31, face up, and fire up the channel.
4. Test once whether the four-edge pattern grows the piece back. If it does, travel to the socket at full size; otherwise go as 2×2.

I'll avoid any action that doesn't directly serve this route.

Its beam from x=29 failed twice, and x=33 doesn't cover the channel. The only shot that worked was the shrunk piece at x=31, facing up. Facing comes from the last move. So the route must include shrink (4 clicks) and fire (3 clicks).
- **(c) The refill is necessary.** Without it the budget is about 18 actions. The cheapest route without it needs about 24 (13 moves plus 11 clicks).
- **(d) The refill route is the cheapest.** With the refill, the cheapest route I found is 18 moves plus 11 clicks, about 29 actions:
  - 6 moves to put the shrunk piece on the refill;
  - 5 moves to stand under the channel facing up, at the height that regrows into the gate row;
  - 7 moves to the socket at x57.

  The alternatives cost the same or more: staying shrunk (13 moves instead of grow plus 7), regrowing to line up a full-size shot, firing before refilling (the timer empties first), and shrinking at the start.
- **(e) The budget is about 26 actions.** Two identical runs of that route died on action 26.

What it rests on: (a), the movement grid, the shrink/grow anchoring, the refill amount and the death point are all observed. The route minimisation is my own hand enumeration, not an exhaustive search.

What I haven't checked:
- whether a full-size beam at x31 works (reachable only through shrink and regrow, and still longer);
- whether partially entering the socket wins (saves at most 1 move);
- whether the beam can collect the refill from a distance;
- the panel combinations I didn't try.

Because the level was presumably built to be solvable, I suspect a missing mechanic.

**3. Rules newly worked out, and from what**

- **Panel patterns:** clicking cells in the 3×3 panel triggers an effect when the selection exactly matches a shown pattern. I saw this when selecting all four edges shrank the piece on level 1. A superset selection didn't fire until I removed the extra cell.
- **Pattern effects:** the four edges shrink the piece, and repeating them grows it back (observed). The middle column fires a beam in the direction of the last move until it hits a wall (seen in the beam animations). On level 2, one pattern teleported the piece into a marked area.
- **Breaking the box opens the gate:** seen on level 3, and on level 4 once the shrunk piece was aligned.
- **Shrink and grow anchoring:** shrinking keeps the top-left quarter, whatever the facing; tested facing right, down and left. Growing turns the shrunk piece into the bottom-right quarter, seen at two places.
- **Refill:** the `ee` item is collected only by the shrunk piece overlapping it, and gives about 36 timer rows. The full-size piece covering it did nothing, twice; the shrunk piece dropped the timer from 52 to 20 and from 38 to 2.
- **Free clicks:** clicking the pattern boxes on the left is free and only marks the pattern's cells. Clicking elsewhere flashes the panel red and also costs nothing.

**4. Still unsure**

- **The beam's hit rule.** I don't know whether a full-size beam fails because only one half of it counts, or because the target box must span all of the piece's columns. The level 3 success and the level 4 failures can't tell these apart.
- **Exact timer costs.** Moves read as 3.2–3.6 rows each, and pattern-completing clicks as about 6. Per-action rounding in the bar's display could be hiding a cheaper action type.
- **Partial socket entry.** On level 1 the win seemed to come on partial entry. I never tested that on level 4.
- **A missing mechanic.** I'm unsure whether one exists at all, since my arithmetic says the level can't be done as I understand it.
